**Estimating project tasks**

technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as extensions to the existing Spring-based XD/CF runtime rather than introducing a separate service.
Implement the RxJava capability as a reusable processor module with non-blocking stream processing, configurable backpressure, and lifecycle management integrated with the existing module model.
Treat U4 and U5 as duplicate requirements and implement one HDFS-backed custom-module uber-jar capability.
Use the Hadoop FileSystem abstraction for HDFS access, with atomic temporary-file upload followed by rename to make publication resilient to partial writes.
Make the HDFS location and YARN configuration location externally configurable through existing CF/runtime configuration mechanisms, with validated defaults.

Implement Spark job termination through the existing Spark submission or cluster-management integration, using an idempotent stop operation and reporting meaningful errors when the job no longer exists.
Limit ACL work to the requested discovery and design spike: customer-use-case analysis, XD-runtime approach evaluation, DSL/UI scope, and phased next-step documentation.

Perform CPU-startup investigation using representative admin and container startup profiles and document bottlenecks, causes, and remediation trade-offs rather than implementing speculative optimizations.
Use the project's existing build, logging, exception, configuration, and test conventions and target Java 17 or newer.
assumptions: The existing codebase already contains module lifecycle management, CF configuration support, Spark integration points, and Hadoop client dependencies that can be extended.
The estimate covers one developer performing analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, and local integration validation; it excludes elapsed waiting time for external teams or environments.
No production deployment, operational rollout, migration of existing stored jars, or long-running performance test campaign is included.
HDFS authentication, HA Namenode configuration, and YARN cluster availability are provided by the existing deployment environment.
The HDFS feature stores and retrieves one custom module uber-jar per module/version using a deterministic configurable path.
Configuration overrides require validation, documentation, and automated tests but do not require a new UI unless the existing configuration framework already exposes one.
ACL implementation is not included because U2 explicitly defines a spike scope rather than a finished enforcement feature.
The performance investigation has access to representative startup scenarios and profiling tools, but any code changes resulting from the investigation are out of scope.
The increment requires unit and integration tests for changed behavior, with external HDFS, YARN, and Spark systems represented by test doubles where a live environment is unavailable.
Estimates include normal code review preparation and defect correction discovered during the planned validation, but not major redesign caused by undocumented legacy behavior.

activities.activity_description: Review existing module, processor, configuration, HDFS/YARN, Spark, testing, and documentation structures; map each story to extension points and define implementation sequencing.

activities.activity_name: RxJava processor module design and implementation
activities.activity_description: Define the processor API and lifecycle behavior, add RxJava integration, implement reactive processing and error/backpressure handling, and integrate the module with the existing runtime.

Review representative customer use cases, evaluate ACL approaches compatible with the XD runtime, define resource/user privilege concepts, identify DSL and UI scope, and document recommended phases and next steps.
Create reproducible admin and container startup scenarios, collect profiles, identify CPU bottlenecks, document likely causes, and record optimization alternatives with pros and cons.
Implement configurable HDFS upload, retrieval, existence checks, atomic publication, failure handling, and reinstall/read behavior for custom module uber-jars in HA scenarios.

activities.activity_name: CF HDFS and YARN configuration overrides
activities.activity_description: Add CF-user-overridable HDFS storage location and YARN configuration location, including precedence rules, validation, defaults, propagation to runtime components, and configuration error reporting.
Add an API or command path to stop an existing Spark job, integrate with the current Spark submission/cluster client, make the operation idempotent, and handle completed, missing, and failed jobs.

Add tests for RxJava processing, HDFS persistence and failure recovery, configuration overrides, Spark termination, validation, and relevant ACL/profiling deliverables; use mocks or local substitutes for external systems.
Run the complete increment through representative module installation, HA-style HDFS recovery, CF configuration, Spark cleanup, and startup profiling scenarios; resolve defects and regressions.
Document configuration properties, operational behavior, limitations, ACL spike recommendations, profiling findings, test results, and release notes; prepare the final change set.
